conclusions: The integral over the real line of exp(lambda x) with respect to gaussianReal(0, 1) equals exp(lambda squared divided by 2).
mathematical_definitions: Let mu denote gaussianReal(0, 1), the real measure obtained from the nonzero branch of gaussianReal, namely real volume measure weighted by gaussianPDF(0, 1).
The integrand is the real-valued function x mapped to exp(lambda x).
The left-hand side is the real Bochner integral of that integrand with respect to mu.
The right-hand side is the real exponential of lambda squared divided by the real number 2.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every real number lambda, integrating exp(lambda x) against the Gaussian measure constructed with parameters 0 and 1 gives exactly exp(lambda squared over 2).

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition concerns only the single measure gaussianReal(0, 1); it does not state a formula for arbitrary Gaussian parameters.

There is no implication and no potentially inconsistent premise, so there is no ordinary logical vacuity risk.
